factors.label: Switzerland: consumption mix incl. imports (location-based)
factors.source: BFE/treeze electricity label, consumer mix 2021–2023: 111 g fossil CO2/kWh at the low-voltage socket (pubdb.bfe.admin.ch); VSE strom.ch «CO2-Gehalt des Strommix Schweiz» based on the BAFU Scope Emissions Tool: 57–59 g CO2e/kWh for 2024, 90 g for 2025 (preliminary); BAFU/treeze «Umweltbilanz Strommix Schweiz»: consumer mix 128 g CO2e/kWh; Empa: ~108 g incl. imports. Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: CHOICE: consumption mix incl. imports, not production mix. A Zurich data centre draws electricity from the grid as it is, imports included (Switzerland imports in winter, largely from DE/FR). The production mix (~30 g) would ignore those imports and understate the footprint about fourfold. mid = BFE consumer mix (111 g, rounded to 0.110), low = VSE 2024 (57 g, a year with high hydro), high = BAFU consumer mix (128 g).

factors.label: Germany (Frankfurt): national electricity mix
factors.source: Umweltbundesamt, «Entwicklung der spezifischen Treibhausgas-Emissionen des deutschen Strommix 1990–2024» (Climate Change 13/2025) and UBA topic page «CO2-Emissionen pro Kilowattstunde Strom 2024»: 363 g CO2/kWh in 2024 (estimate), 386 g in 2023. Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: mid = UBA 2024 (direct CO2 of electricity consumed in Germany). low = ~2025 level (UBA: slightly lower than 2024). high = 2022-like level (433 g) / life-cycle upstream emissions on top of direct CO2.

factors.label: Ireland (Dublin): national electricity mix
factors.source: EPA Ireland, Provisional Greenhouse Gas Emissions 1990–2024: power generation intensity 226 g CO2/kWh in 2024 (254 g in 2023); Electricity Maps «Grid in review 2025 – Ireland»: 352 g CO2e/kWh mean 2024 (life-cycle, flow-traced). Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: mid = EPA 2024 (production-based, direct). high = Electricity Maps life-cycle flow-traced value (includes imports and upstream). low = continuing trend (−10 %/year).

factors.label: EU-27 average (AI providers and SaaS: location «EU (mixed)», not specified)
factors.source: Ember, European Electricity Review 2025: EU-27 power sector intensity 213 g CO2/kWh in 2024. data_center_locations.csv: AI provider (API) «EU (mixed)», location not specified. Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: Location unknown inside the EU → EU average. Range spans likely host countries (Nordics/France lower, Germany/Netherlands/Ireland higher).

factors.label: PUE Azure / AWS data centres
factors.source: Cloud Carbon Footprint methodology (cloudcarbonfootprint.org/docs/methodology): AWS 1.135, Azure 1.185 (provider-declared); Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2025: industry weighted average 1.54. Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: mid = provider-declared values (~1.16–1.19). How far to trust them: they are fleet-wide design/annual figures published by the providers themselves, not per site, not audited per region; so the high end uses the industry average 1.54 as a conservative bound.

factors.label: PUE Swiss hoster (small colocation, no published value)
factors.source: Uptime Institute Global Data Center Survey 2025 (average 1.54; Europe among the lowest regions). Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: No published PUE for the hoster → industry average as mid, wider range.

factors.label: Energy per vCPU-hour (at 50 % CPU, incl. 2 GB memory)
factors.source: Cloud Carbon Footprint methodology: average min/max W per vCPU AWS 0.74/3.5, Azure 0.78/3.76 (mid = mean), memory 0.392 W per GB; default utilisation 50 % when not measured. Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: (Wmin + u × (Wmax − Wmin) + 2 GB × W/GB) / 1000; the engine uses the observed CPU utilisation of each line instead of 50 %. low/high = ±30–40 % around the CCF averages for newer / older processor generations.

factors.label: Energy per node-hour (16 vCPU, 64 GB, at 50 % CPU)
factors.source: Cloud Carbon Footprint methodology: average min/max W per vCPU AWS 0.74/3.5, Azure 0.78/3.76 (mid = mean), memory 0.392 W per GB; default utilisation 50 % when not measured. Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: (16 × W per vCPU + 64 GB × W/GB) / 1000; observed utilisation per line in the engine

factors.label: Energy per GPU-hour (300-W class at 10 % GPU, incl. host)
factors.source: data_dictionary.md (300-W class GPU); idle 10–30 % of TDP is an assumption for data-centre GPUs.
factors.calculation: W = idle + u_gpu × (300 − idle) + host (8 vCPU at host CPU utilisation + 56 GB memory). Shown at 10 % GPU / 5 % host CPU (observed level); the engine uses the weekly measured GPU utilisation.

factors.label: Energy per GB-day of storage
factors.source: Cloud Carbon Footprint methodology: HDD 0.65 Wh/TB-h, SSD 1.2 Wh/TB-h; replication factor up to 3. Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: low = HDD, no replication: 0.65 Wh/TB-h × 24 h / 1000 = 0.0156 Wh/GB-day; mid = HDD × 3 replicas; high = SSD × 3 replicas (1.2 × 3 × 24 / 1000 = 0.0864 Wh/GB-day).

factors.label: Energy per GB transferred
factors.source: Cloud Carbon Footprint methodology: 0.001 kWh/GB; Aslan et al. (2018), Journal of Industrial Ecology: 0.06 kWh/GB in 2015, halving about every two years (→ ~0.002 by 2025). Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: mid = Aslan trend extrapolated to 2025; low = CCF; high = conservative (older access networks).

factors.label: Energy per 1000 output-equivalent tokens (large model)
factors.source: Google (Aug 2025, arXiv 2508.15734): median Gemini text prompt 0.24 Wh fully loaded (0.10 Wh counting only active accelerators); Epoch AI (2025): ~0.3 Wh per typical ChatGPT query (~500 output tokens); OpenAI CEO (Jun 2025): 0.34 Wh average query. ML.ENERGY leaderboard for open models. Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: 0.24–0.34 Wh for a prompt with a few hundred output tokens → ~0.5 Wh per 1000 output tokens (mid). low = active-accelerator-only figure; high = long context / reasoning models / less efficient serving. Output-equivalent tokens = output + 0.1 × uncached input + 0.01 × cached input. Fully loaded → no PUE on top.

factors.label: Energy per message in an AI subscription
factors.source: Google (Aug 2025): 0.24 Wh median prompt, 0.10 Wh active-only; Epoch AI (2025): ~0.3 Wh typical query, up to ~2.5 Wh with long inputs; OpenAI CEO (Jun 2025): 0.34 Wh. Retrieved 2026-11-21.
factors.calculation: Per message in Copilot / ChatGPT Team / Claude Team; fully loaded → no PUE on top.

factors.label: Energy per active SaaS licence-month
factors.source: Team assumption (bottom-up), no public per-licence figure; documented as an estimate.
factors.calculation: Multi-tenant SaaS: ~0.05 vCPU continuously per active user (0.05 × 730 h × ~3 W ≈ 0.11 kWh) + ~10 GB storage (≈ 0.014 kWh) ≈ 0.12 kWh IT energy, × PUE ≈ 0.15 kWh per active licence-month. Unused licences cost money but add almost no energy in a multi-tenant service → energy counts active licences only.
